committee_name.text: Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC)

quote.quote: On November 19, 2013, the Division sought advice from the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) regarding the appropriateness of the 6MWT to assess treatment benefit in this patient population.
A meeting of the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee was convened on November 19, 2013 to discuss the efficacy and safety of elosulfase.

recommendation.text: The majority voted for approval in all MPS IVA patients: 18 members voted for approval in all patients, 2 for approval in a subgroup, and 1 against approval.

quote.quote: Eighteen EMDAC members voted for approval of Vimizim in all patients with MPS IVA; two voted for approval for a subgroup of MPS IVA patients; and one voted against approval.

linkages.concern: AC members were concerned about the long-term durability of the treatment effect of elosulfase alfa, and noted the pivotal 6MWT result may not fully capture clinically meaningful benefit over time.
linkages.change: Approval was granted with required postmarketing studies to demonstrate long-term clinical benefit (durability) and safety of the drug.

concern_quote.quote: AC members were concerned about the long term durability of effect with elosulfase alfa treatment.

change_quote.quote: This reviewer recommends approval of BLA 125460 with the requirement for postmarketing studies to demonstrate long-term clinical benefit and safety with use of the drug product.

summary: An Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) meeting was held on November 19, 2013, convened chiefly to confirm whether the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) was an adequate, clinically meaningful efficacy endpoint for MPS IVA. The committee largely validated the application: the majority found the 6MWT adequate and voted for approval (18 for approval in all patients, 2 for a subgroup, 1 against), and the majority saw no major safety concerns. The committee did not drive major changes to the approval; its concern about the long-term durability of effect aligns with (but is not explicitly tied in the reviews to) the review team's requirement for postmarketing studies of long-term benefit and safety.
